newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM withdraws insurance regulatory bill.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM withdraws insurance regulatory bill.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Wednesday withdrew an insurance regulatory bill from the lower house of parliament after his coalition failed to muster enough votes to defeat an opposition-backed amendment.

"We withdraw the bill," Gujral told the lower house, the Lok Sabha, after Speaker P.A. Sangma rejected the prime minister's request to defer a vote on the amendment, which would have barred multinational companies from the insurance sector.

The bill would create the Insurance Regulatory Authority to oversee the state-controlled insurance industry, and is considered an important first step towards the eventual opening up of the sector to private competition, both Indian and foreign.

Earlier on Wednesday, the lower house rejected an amendment proposed by the Communist Party of India-Marxist, which is part of Gujral's coalition, to bar private firms from the insurance sector. The amendment was defeated by a 228-to-43 vote in the 545-seat house.
The government proposed in the 1997/98 (April-March) budget to open the health insurance sector to a small number of private Indian companies.

But the government was unable to rally enough supporters to defeat the amendment, proposed by the rightwing opposition Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which would bar multinational firms from insurance.
